user_story: As a cook, I want to keep track of store orders so that I can schedule orders.
plantuml:
Here is the sequence diagram for the given user story:


@startuml
actor Cook
participant StoreOrders
database OrderDatabase

Cook -> OrderDatabase: Retrieve store orders
OrderDatabase --> Cook: Confirm retrieval of store orders

Cook -> StoreOrders: Monitor store order status
StoreOrders --> Cook: Receive updates on store order status

Cook -> OrderDatabase: Update order status in database
OrderDatabase --> Cook: Confirm update of order status

@enduml

user_story: As a Data Consuming User, I want to be able to search any dataset published and publicly accessible by their title and metadata, So that I can find the datasets I'm interested in.
plantuml:
Here is a sequence diagram for the given user story:

```plantuml
@startuml
data consuming user->dataset repository:search by title 
dataset repository->dataset repository:return search results 
data consuming user->system:select dataset from results 
@enduml
```

In this sequence diagram, the `data consuming user` initiates a search for datasets in the `dataset repository` using their title. The `dataset repository` then returns a list of search results to the `data consuming user`, who can select a desired dataset from the results.

user_story: As a library member, I want to locate related books and see the shelf number in the library by using unique information to speed up the searching process.
plantuml:
Here is the sequence diagram for the given user story:

```plantuml
@startuml
actor LibraryMember
participant SearchEngine
participant CatalogSystem
participant ShelfLocator

LibraryMember ->> SearchEngine: Input unique book information to search
SearchEngine --> CatalogSystem: Query catalog system for related books and shelf number
CatalogSystem --> SearchEngine: Retrieve list of related books with shelf numbers
SearchEngine --> LibraryMember: Display results to library member

SearchEngine -> ShelfLocator: Get shelf information from shelf locator module
ShelfLocator --> SearchEngine: Return shelf number for selected book

@enduml
```

This sequence diagram represents the interactions between a library member, search engine, catalog system, and shelf locator to facilitate efficient searching of related books in the library.

user_story: As an API User, I want to be able to use data to get results from multiple datasets, So that I can build user experiences based on more than one dataset more easily.
plantuml:
Here is a sequence diagram for the given user story:

```plantuml
@startuml
api_user->System:use data 
System-->data_service1: get data from dataset1
System-->data_service2: get data from dataset2
data_service1-->System:return valid_data1
data_service2-->System:return valid_data2
System-->api_user:return results
@enduml
```

This sequence diagram shows the interaction between the API User and the System, where the System uses data services to retrieve data from multiple datasets (dataset1 and dataset2) and returns the results to the API User.

user_story: As a customer, I want to be able to pay the bill partially
plantuml:
Here is a sequence diagram for the given user story:


@startuml
actor Customer
participant PaymentGateway
participant OrderService

Customer -> OrderService: Request partial payment of bill
OrderService --> Customer: Confirm request for partial payment

OrderService -> PaymentGateway: Process partial payment
PaymentGateway --> OrderService: Confirm successful payment

OrderService -> OrderService: Update order with partial payment
OrderService --> Customer: Notify customer of partial payment update

@enduml

user_story: As a cook, I want to have employee data on the system including clock in and out information.
plantuml:
Here is the sequence diagram based on the given user story:

```plantuml
@startuml
actor Cook
database EmployeeDatabase
participant TimeTracker

Cook -> TimeTracker: Request employee data including clock in/out info
TimeTracker --> EmployeeDatabase: Retrieve employee details and time records
EmployeeDatabase --> TimeTracker: Provide valid employee data
TimeTracker --> Cook: Display employee information, clock in/out times

activate Cook
deactivate Cook

@enduml
```

This sequence diagram illustrates the interaction between a `Cook` actor requesting employee data and time records, and the system's components (`TimeTracker` participant) retrieving this data from the `EmployeeDatabase`.
